title: DNA Extraction Protocol for Genome Sequencing
author: Isabelle Vea
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.pvgdn3w
materials: From fresh whole sample: Add 3-15 adult females to a 1.5ml Eppendorf tube and add 360μl of Cell Lysis Buffer. Carefully crush females until homogenized. DNA extraction for Illumina sequencing on B chromosome lines: managed to extract DNA from 1 small female (that started to lay eggs). Also tried on 3 females. From frozen whole: Transfer frozen tubes on dry ice with a pestle, crush carefully on dry ice Add 360 uL of Cell Lysis Buffer (Qiagen) and crush again with the same pestle to continue homogenizing From frozen dissected tissue: Take out tube from storage and add 360 uL of Cell Lysis Buffer (Qiagen)

Allow sample to cool down to RT. Add 4μl of RNase A (From Qiagen kit: 100 mg/ml), mix by inversion and rotation, spin down and incubate for 10 min at room temperature. Andres protocol: 2 min at room temperature for 4uL of RNase A in 400 uL of buffer+PK (1 mg/mL). Dom protocol: 1 hour at 37deg for 4uL RNase A in >610uL of buffer+PK (about 0.65 mg/mL of RNase A) B chromosome line DNA extraction: I incubated at room temperature for 10 min BUT ended up having RNA left, so had to go for a second round of RNase (incubation at 37 deg for 30 min with RNase A 10mg/ml for a sample that had 40ng/uL and 40 ng/uL of RNA after the first round of RNase.) all other samples had < 15 ng/uL of DNA and no RNA left

Whole samples: Transfer live sample to a 1.5 Eppendorf tube, label and close lid Put the tube in liquid nitrogen and leave until it doesn't bubble anymore Store immediately at -80 Dissected tissue (Dom's protocol): Flick sample tubes so that tissue/pellet is NOT located at the bottom of the tube pestles will not reach the bottom more force can be applied if the tissue/pellet is on the side of the tube Freeze tubes in liquid nitrogen; for each tube do: Open tube carefully without breaking off the lid if a lid becomes damaged proceed until step 6, then transfer sample to new tube Crush tissue/pellet using a white/blue pestle through twisting stop once tissue/pellet defrosts keep pestle in rack afterwards do not let the tip of the pestle touch anything besides the sample Freeze tube again (liquid nitrogen) and repeat from 2 [* add 10% by volume 0.5 M EDTA if storing at this point] Tissue dissection in Qiagen buffer: 1. Dissect and move to low quantity buffer (for batches) on ice (not dry ice) 2. Storage?

steps.title: Preheat incubation device
steps.instruction: Set the heat block, water bath, or hot chamber with rocking system to 56 °C.

steps.title: Add Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Pipette 40 µL of Proteinase K (Qiagen, 20 mg/mL) into the sample tube.

steps.title: Add Protein Precipitation Solution and chill
steps.instruction: Add 133 µL of Protein Precipitation Solution (Qiagen) to the sample, mix by inversion and rotation, spin down briefly, then incubate on ice for at least 10 min (vortex 20 s and chill 10 min; B‑chromosome line: 20 min on ice). The sample may be stored at –20 °C at this point.

steps.title: First centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 10 min at 13,000 rpm at 4 °C (B‑chromosome line: 15 min).

steps.title: Transfer supernatant and add isopropanol
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the clear supernatant to a new tube, avoiding the white precipitate, then add 400 µL of isopropanol (B‑chromosome line: typically 450 µL transferred).

steps.title: Mix and spin down
steps.instruction: Mix the solution gently by inversion until a visible DNA mass forms, then spin down briefly.

steps.title: Second centrifugation and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 10 min at 13,000 rpm at 4 °C, then discard the supernatant quickly by inverting the tube.

steps.title: Ethanol wash of DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL of 70 % ethanol, detach the DNA pellet from the tube wall (pipette if large), invert several times to wash, then centrifuge for 30 min at 13,000 rpm at 4 °C (Andrés protocol: 5 min after wash). Aspirate the ethanol with a pipette (do not discard by inversion). Use freshly prepared 70 % ethanol kept on ice to prevent evaporation.

steps.title: Repeat ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Repeat the ethanol‑wash step at least once more until the pellet appears white (note that pellets may be very small with low tissue amounts).

steps.title: Air‑dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Invert the tube onto tissue paper and air‑dry the pellet under the hood for 10–15 min or until it becomes transparent (check after 15 min; Dom’s protocol uses 1 h).

steps.title: Elute DNA in TE buffer
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of TE buffer or Qiagen Elution Buffer. Rehydrate the DNA by incubating overnight at room temperature or 4 °C. Alternative incubations: overnight at 56 °C in a heated chamber with rocking, or overnight at –20 °C (or ≥10 min on dry ice if overnight incubation is not possible).

steps.title: Post‑incubation handling
steps.instruction: After the incubation, remove the sample from the heated chamber, spin down, then mix by inversion and rotation and spin down again in a micro‑centrifuge (do not mix vigorously).

steps.title: Quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Take 1 µL of the eluate for a Nanodrop measurement (A260/280 should be 1.7–1.8; >1.8 indicates RNA contamination). Check the 260/230 ratio (values <1 suggest other contaminants; run a purification kit if needed). Also determine DNA (and RNA) concentrations with a Qubit fluorometer.
